Permits are stacked and things don't look bad visually. There does seem to be a margin issue with the gradient overlay. It's most noticeable at the bottom of the screen and grows if you have a vertical console and drag it
I'm able to claim each permit so long as they are all on the same network. The NFT permits are stacked and the additional details look okay
EDIT:
I didn't QA mobile manually but will do on the next pass

Overall I think the code looks good other than two little things.
I will give things a proper going over tomorrow

Overall great work with this
After making a few changes to get things working (addressed in comments) I manually QA'd with two permits from different networks and things work but there a few bugs although they can be addressed with other issues once merged (since multi-network permits aren't in use right now)
Sorry for the slow review it slipped my mind, please ping me after a day or two in the future if it happens again.

I think this is good to merge following any other review comments
- Dual network permits work (I can post a video if needed)
- permits are stacked and all functions work
- Manually QA'd mobile and the only comment is that you only see one permit above the fold and it's not immediately clear that you can scroll or that you have more than one
- The known issue with MM browser and us switching the user network is still present so while multi-network permits work on mobile they need to change their network manually. (For mobile QA I did not fire any txs but I did receive the relevant wallet prompts for them. That's because it's difficult to work with anvil and mm mobile)

Neither `Permit` or `ERC20Permit` are exported from this package which essentially casts everything as `any`. The correct import is `PermitReward` or `Erc20PermitReward` and using these creates ts errors regarding using `bigint (nonce)` for indexing objects.
This issue has already been resolved although we haven't pushed a new release yet I believe although imports from `/dist` will produce the types but that change has to be made while the server is running as they are not exported from there and build would fail.
`currentExplorerUrl` doesn't exist on the `claim` object
Because this is cast as `any` due to the import issue you haven't noticed you are still passing `app` to this function instead of the claim so this function throws
the claim/reward object does not have `currentExplorerUrl` all usage of this needs refactored
If we have multiple permits with different networks they'd only be able claim those that are on the same network as `claim[0]`
you are still using `app.networkId` in this file but it's been removed from `app`
With stacked permits this check would need to be added into the claim flow so that we confirm the network for each potentially different claim

You call `renderTransaction()` while creating each new table so this will fire multiple network change prompts from MM if multiple networks exist and ultimately it'll prevent at least one permit from being claimed
you should use `app.getCurrentExplorerUrl()` so there's a fallback
we should connect the wallet first and then verify the network. We should also await it before proceeding.
Same here, connect first then verify

You should keep this as `app.signer` is used throughout various functions before clicking `claim` and with this removed you'd need to handle each case with `app.provider.getSigner()`. 
Noticeably with this removed the UI has a hard time detecting when to display the `invalidate claim` button as the connection event happens only once you click claim
Still some usage of `app.networkId` in this file
This loop is running before `app.claims` is set so the buttons don't work unless this runs somewhere after `app.claims` is set.

hi @pbkompasz, the tests are the expected behaviour buddy
Your first run 3 days ago [passed](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/actions/runs/10275022156/job/28432892698) and all other [runs](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/actions/workflows/cypress-testing.yml) pass just fine. Can you link to the run which has failed as I cannot seem to find it.
The most recent cypress run [passed](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/actions/runs/10318208459/job/28564086984) too. Maybe you meant that it was CI that had failed on `development`?
I will add my review once the requested changes are made

I figured that since all these tables you have created are self-contained then they should also contain what's needed to fire the tx for that permit. It makes sense to me to place it inside the claim flow then it's handled elegantly and easily rather than it being a global-access provider which may not apply to all permits.
We aim to support any and all (EVM) networks and have been building with that in mind in every other area so I thought it applied here. If it's too much work it can be addressed when it's required I guess.

Something like that yeah. If all of these checks are performed at the click of the claim button or mid-claim-flow for that specific permit then you have all you need from the `permit` object to validate networks etc.
I wouldn't check each network is added because it will prompt the user to actually switch their network. I'd expect with multiple permits in view you'd only be prompted to switch network after clicking claim _if_ your network didn't match the current network. Does that make sense? 
But again, if it's too much just roll with a single network provider. You have done a superb job so far and we can always task this out once it's required.
